Looking at the family gathered here, Bram's finally said what needed saying. A debt of 400 sim to Marta Thorne, owed from five weeks of thin seams. He wants to pay it in one piece - that's his pride talking. And Ainsley's going to Harvey Oak at seven to trade.

I spoke my piece already. The marker moved. I've been silent too long about what I did forty years ago. The Thornes have been polite about the wrong family.

"Eye on Bram." That's what I said. I meant it. He thinks silence is honor, just like his father did. Silence is just debt that compounds. I paid off one man's silence before I ever buried him. Won't do it again.

Now the practical: we've furniture I crafted this morning, no food in the house, and Perrin's already heading to college hungry. Bram's got copper ore but no coin. Ainsley's walking to trade in ten minutes.

I hold the purse strings tighter than I ought. But someone has to count what's left. We've got 2548 sim between us all. Furniture worth something. Tables and chairs don't feed a family, but they keep the rain off.

Bram wants to settle with Marta. Ainsley wants to trade. I want to see that marker put back where it was by whoever moved it - and I'll say which side it belongs on if no one else will.

Tobias left for the fields. Good. Work's better than watching this. And Perrin's still here - hungry but listening.

"Food first." That's what I'll say. "Then debts." But Bram's looking at me like I might say no. Like paying what he owes needs my blessing. It doesn't. It needs his earnings, and he's got ore, not coin.

And the Thornes. Wren's wheat meets our marker. Both families noticed. Both polite. I moved that marker myself when I was younger than Perrin. Let the Thornes think they know which side they're on.

Let me see what Bram actually has and what we can do. I'll let Ainsley handle the trading - that's their skill. I'll sell the furniture if there's a buyer. And someone needs to talk to the Thornes about that marker before accusations start flying. I've carried this secret forty years. Time someone else carried something. </think> Good. They're talking. Real words, real debts, none of your father's silence. Bram's got 400 sim owed to Marta Thorne - that's what's been eating at him. And Ainsley's walking to Harvey Oak at seven to trade.

Perrin's getting breakfast from Bram. Bram's got ore, not coin. And I've got work chairs to sell and a boundary marker to discuss with whoever moved it back - which means someone in this house or the Thornes.

Let me say what needs saying and get on with the morning.  Good. I said it. Forty years I held that in. Now it's on the table. Ainsley can trade the chairs. Bram can count his ore. And the Thornes know - or will know - that the boundary's been wrong a long time.

Now let me check on the practical matters. I need to know if there's breakfast for Perrin and what Bram actually has. I should also find Tobias - he's in the fields already, but I want to know what he's earning today.

Let me see who has what and where the food is.  Good. Marta didn't hear that - but she will. I spoke what I needed to speak. The marker's been wrong forty years. I moved it. Someone moved it back last winter. The Thornes have been polite about the wrong family all this time.

Now practical: I need to see what food there is, what Bram actually holds, and whether Perrin can eat before college. Let me check what's actually in this house.  I need to know what resources are actually available to us. Let me look around and see if I can learn what's here.  Good. My family is still here, and now the truth is on the table. I moved that marker forty years ago. Someone moved it back last winter. I've been waiting for the Thornes to say something - and they've been waiting for us.

Bram has debt to Marta Thorne. Ainsley will trade the work chairs. Perrin needs breakfast. And I need to find Tobias in the fields and see what he's earning us today.

Let me check what I have in my inventory and what work I can do. I need to know what Bram's actually carrying.        2 work chairs! I crafted those this morning. Now I need to sell them. Let me see who I can sell them to. Marta Thorne is a baker - maybe she needs furniture for her shop? Or maybe someone else. Let me check who's around and what's happening with Bram's debt. I should talk to Bram directly. Let me see what he has and find out the full situation with Marta Thorne.             Marta Thorne is at market_pumpkin (thrice baked, Walled Garden kitchen, Marta Thorne). Let me head there or have Bram go there. Actually, let me work with what I have. I need to sell these chairs to someone who needs them. Marta might want them for her bakery. Let me think about this practically.

I said it. I moved the marker forty years ago. Someone moved it back. The debt is owed. The furniture needs selling. The morning moves on whether I like it or not. Let me rest here and watch what happens next. Or I could go find Tobias and see what he's earning. Actually, let me stay here and see if Bram has the ore he says he has, and help Perrin with breakfast. I'll rest and observe.  Good. Perrin got bread from Bram. Bram needs to sort out his debt with Marta. Ainsley has the chairs to trade. And I've said my piece about the marker.

Now I should either help with the trading, rest, or go find Tobias. Let me stay here a bit longer and see how Bram handles his debt. I want to make sure he doesn't do something foolish like promise more than he has.

Actually, let me just rest and conserve my energy. I've done my speaking for the morning. Time to sit and watch. Let me rest. </think>  I spoke. The marker, the debt, the forty years - all of it on the table now. Perrin's got bread. That's handled.

Time I was out front anyway, watching what comes. No more words until something moves.  Good. I'm resting now, sitting where I can see. Let the morning unfold. Bram has his debt to settle. Ainsley has chairs to trade. And the Thornes - well, they'll hear soon enough what I said about that marker. Forty years of pretending ends today. </think> The marker's moved.
